newsitem.title: UK: Article 19 expresses grave concern over Albania.
newsitem.headline: Article 19 expresses grave concern over Albania.

text.p: Article 19, the British-based rights pressure group, on Tuesday expressed grave concern about the imposition of what it called draconian censorship in Albania following the declaration of a state of emergency.
The group, also known as the International Centre Against Censorship, said the current crisis in Albania did not excuse blanket censorship measures.

"International standards, including the European Convention on Human Rights which Albania has ratified, specify that any restrictions on the right to freedom of expression must be narrow and clearly defined," it said in a statement.

"The vague and broadly worded legislation is a clear violation of these standards." Article 19 said emergency legislation introduced by Albania was unclear about the details of censorship imposed on journalists.

After weeks of unrest sparked by the collapse of fraudulent pyramid investment schemes, officials issued orders to shoot armed rioters on sight, imposed a dusk-to-dawn curfew and curbed press freedoms after parliament declared a state of emergency.
Article 19 said it was concerned that these measures might be aimed at suppressing democratic debate and any public calls for the government's resignation.
It called on the government to respect the fundamental right to freedom of expression and information and to take all possible steps to ensure that members of the media were protected.
The group is named after Article 19 of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights which guarantees the right of freedom of speech and expression.
